title: AI Engineer or ML Engineer? Pick Wrong and It Costs You
description:
AI engineer versus ML engineer. They sound like the same job. They are not. One of these roles gets the big checks, the other one gets the door open.

I break down what each one actually does all day. One ships products on a model someone else already trained. The other builds it, trains it and deploys it. I've run Claude agents across whole pipelines and I never actually trained a model, so I know my side.

Then how to choose: your background, whether you want to train models or ship products, and what the market is hiring for. And the money, on real US pay data. Top 10% versus typical, the gap is around $340,000 a year. Which one are you picking?
